notes: Runner never built a breaker suite able to contest the scoring remote, idled on credit clicks while rich, and ran into a rezzed Piranhas four times in one turn, trashing its own hand for nothing.
Efficient install-and-score tempo won on turn 10, but R&D stayed unprotected for four turns while the Runner multi-ran it and stole Fujii.
Correctly hammered an unprotected R&D every click and won on turn 4.
Good use of Vertigo, Seamless Launch and same-turn scoring for a win, though R&D had only one cheap ice all game and leaked two agendas.
Strong early R&D dig and timely remote steals, with an odd Maintenance Access played and immediately jacked out of.
Kept a single ice on each central all game while the Runner ran them every turn, and clicked for credits at 11-14 credits while discarding instead of icing up; agendas leaked from R&D and HQ.
A steady R&D plan won the game, but economy stayed near zero and Nuka draws overfilled the grip; it also ran into a known Capacitor without the credits to break it.
Clicked for credits nearly every turn up to 67 credits without installing a breaker or playing cards, and only facechecked a few ETR ice while the Corp scored freely.
Never scored, left R&D behind one ice and an agenda in HQ, played Neurospike with no agenda scored that turn, and ran out of credits from midgame.
Left R&D with no ice for four turns while the Runner multi-ran it and took three agendas, then recovered with steady remote scoring against a passive Runner.
Solid economy and layered remote scoring, though the first agenda went into a one-ice remote against a 21-credit Runner and was stolen.
Good remote pressure and steady steals against a broke Corp, with a couple of costly facechecks (lost Buzzsaw and Fencer) and tags left floating.
Spent about eight turns clicking for credits up to 31 while discarding every turn, never punishing a tagged Runner and not installing anything; Embedded Reporting was stolen from HQ.

Repeatedly ran into an already-rezzed, unbreakable Vampyronassa and Anemone and jacked out each time, shredding its own hand and credits, then skipped the final Konjin-only remote that held the winning agenda.
Clean aggressive play that broke Hafrún every turn and won on turn 5.
Kept a single cheap ice on R&D while the Runner ran it every turn and spent late ice on campaign remotes instead; agendas leaked from HQ and R&D.

For about fourteen turns it ran only Archives and paid to clear a Trickster Taka tag every turn, never pressuring HQ or R&D while the Corp sat at 0 credits; it won only through agendas the Corp discarded to Archives.
Put agendas in thin remotes against a well-funded Runner, kept agendas in a one-ice HQ and played with almost no money, losing on turn 5.
Shaky early economy and light R&D ice, but recovered with campaigns and a double-Ansel remote that closed the game.
Clicked for credits up to 38 for most of the game while holding a full grip and almost never ran the centrals; it won only because the Corp left Next Big Thing in an unprotected remote.
